change_summary: PLOS ONE retracted the paper because it was identified as one of a series of submissions with concerns about peer review integrity and potential manipulation of the publication process. The editors say these concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results, and that the author either did not respond directly or could not be reached. The retraction covers the whole paper and casts doubt on its reported results, so its findings cannot be relied on.
evaluation: Your Section 3 calls Dutta [14] "the main evidence" for choosing an LSTM and relies on its reported LURL accuracy, which the stored paper gives as 97.4% and 96.8%. Your Section 4 also starts from the LURL settings in [14], such as hidden size 650 and learning rate 1.0 with decay 0.73. The notice retracts the paper and says the concerns call into question the validity and provenance of the reported results. So the Section 3 argument that relies on the reported accuracy is touched, and so is the Section 4 use of the settings. The impact on your draft is high, since both the main justification for the detector and its starting configuration rest on this paper.
recommendation: Your Section 3 cites Dutta [14] as the main evidence for choosing an LSTM, and the retraction notice questions the validity and provenance of the reported results, so that use is touched. Your Section 4 also starts from the LURL settings in [14], and that use is touched too. Replace or remove the citation in Section 3 and re-check the detector choice. Raise the Section 4 settings with your co-authors or supervisor, since the draft's own method depends on them.
